holidays.name: National Barbie Day
holidays.description: A pink-tinted salute to the iconic fashion doll. Fans dust off their dream-house collections, strike a pose, and toast decades of Barbie careers, from astronaut to president.
holidays.origin: Barbie made her debut at the American International Toy Fair in New York on March 9, 1959. Mattel co-founder Ruth Handler created her and named her after her daughter, Barbara.
holidays.funFact: Barbie's full name is Barbara Millicent Roberts, and Ken is named after Ruth Handler's son.

holidays.name: National Meatball Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble ball of seasoned ground meat. Spaghetti, subs, Swedish-style with gravy, or on a toothpick all count.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its creator is unclear, but it has become a fixture on March 9 calendars.
holidays.funFact: Almost every cuisine has its own version of the meatball, including Italian polpette, Swedish köttbullar, Middle Eastern kofta and Chinese lion's head meatballs.

holidays.name: National Get Over It Day
holidays.description: A day to drop a grudge, shrug off an embarrassment, and move on. It's an annual permission slip to stop dwelling on the little stuff.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It invites people to let go of petty annoyances and start fresh.
holidays.funFact: Researchers who study rumination say that dwelling on a problem tends to make people feel worse, not better. That's good science behind a silly holiday.
